summary: Wire the Quality Gates workflow at .github/workflows so GitHub Actions can run it and required status checks can attach. The gate definition previously existed only as the distributable template at ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml, which GitHub never reads. A Greptile review of the wiring then found a shell injection and three correctness defects in that gate definition; those are fixed here in both copies, because wiring the workflow is what made them live.

rollback_plan: Revert in reverse order. The ownership rule: revert the one added rule in ownership.yaml — one line, under a minute, no data implications; ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml returns to unowned and G-1 reports UNOWNED again instead of FOREIGN. The workflows: `git revert -m 1 <sha>` of the merge, which takes effect on the next workflow dispatch. Data implications: none — the workflows write no state. One caveat: reverting restores ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml to its previous content, which reinstates the shell injection in the distributable template, so a full revert should be paired with either re-applying the env: changes to the template alone or removing the root workflow so nothing executes. Removing just .github/workflows/gates.yml and .github/workflows/gates-template-sync.yml is the safer partial rollback: it stops the gates running while leaving the hardened template in place.

cross_bot_request.protocol: docs/cross-bot-protocol.md — 'request to the owner'. ownership.yaml is not a contracts/ surface, so G-4 and the contract-PR mechanism do not apply; the protocol's other remedy for touching another bot's file is a request to its owner.
cross_bot_request.request: Ratify one added rule: ci/.github/workflows/** -> bot-05-infrastructure.
cross_bot_request.why: The pattern .github/workflows/** is anchored at the repository root and never matched the nested template path, so ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml resolved to no owner. G-1 fails an unowned path for every bot, so no seat could edit the gate template at all — including to fix the shell injection closed in commit a2730a6.
cross_bot_request.why_infra: INFRA already owns .github/workflows/**. The template and the live workflow must always change together, and gates-template-sync.yml fails the build when they drift. Assigning them to different bots would make every future gate change a cross-bot negotiation.
cross_bot_request.status: PENDING — bot-06-quality-security has NOT ratified this. G-1 reports ownership.yaml as FOREIGN for bot-05-infrastructure, and that failure is the intended visible signal, not something to wave past.
cross_bot_request.authorised_by: Repository operator, relayed through the LEAD dispatch for run 20260929T184058Z-e85194ea, after being asked to choose between adding the rule for QUALITY to ratify and waiting for bot-06 to add it.
cross_bot_request.anti_pattern_acknowledged: The protocol lists 'I'll just edit their file, it's a one-liner' as an anti-pattern whose failure mode is being invisible to the owner. This edit is deliberately visible: G-1 blocks on it, this receipt records it, and the pull request asks QUALITY for sign-off. If QUALITY declines, reverting is one line and the template returns to unowned.
cross_bot_request.if_declined: Revert the rule. The gate template then becomes untouchable again, so QUALITY would need to either apply the injection fix to ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml itself under its own seat, or assign that path to some other owner.
